name: Pedro the Lion
label: Jade Tree
lede: A pastor's son wrote Jade Tree's darkest records almost entirely by himself, split his Christian audience with a record about adultery and murder, killed the band, and then brought it back to tell the story of his own childhood.

eras.title: A pastor's son behind the drum kit
eras.text: David Bazan was born in Phoenix, grew up a pastor's son and came up in 1990s Seattle, where Tooth & Nail was selling Christian punk and Built to Spill was rewriting guitar rock. He started Pedro the Lion in 1995 as a project he'd end up writing almost entirely alone.

years.h: David Bazan is born in Phoenix, Arizona
years.p: [[David Bazan|d1714baa-2174-4233-8272-f537bfa9fbba]]'s Arizona childhood would become the subject of Pedro the Lion's comeback album, Phoenix, 43 years later.

years.h: Bazan drums for Damien Jurado, then starts Pedro the Lion
years.p: Bazan played drums in his high school friend [[Damien Jurado|f4805b9d-68f8-438e-8f13-ec7bcb4c8581]]'s band the Guilty, later Coolidge, before forming Pedro the Lion in Seattle in 1995.

years.h: Whole EP on Tooth & Nail, recorded by Seasick Steve
years.p: Steven Gene Wold, later famous as [[Seasick Steve|231ff972-4e8e-4157-95e2-12f963cb478c]], was Bazan's spiritual mentor, played occasional slide guitar and recorded the debut EP.

eras.title: Made in Mexico, raised on Jade Tree
eras.text: A Tooth & Nail publicist started a label just to release Pedro's first album, and Jade Tree picked up the next records. Bazan played nearly everything himself and started writing concept albums about sin and power.

years.h: Big Trucks, a 1,000-copy single on Made in Mexico
years.p: The first Pedro the Lion release on the label Tooth & Nail publicist James Morelos started just for Bazan.

years.cap: It's Hard to Find a Friend, Made in Mexico, 1998
years.h: It's Hard to Find a Friend: a label founded to release it
years.p: James Morelos founded Made in Mexico to put out this album. Bazan sang and played guitar and drums, with Johnathon Ford on bass, all to reel-to-reel tape.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Jeremy Schneyer gave it 7.8 and compared it to Luna. KEXP's Dusty Henry later called it the lushest-sounding recording in Bazan's catalog.

Jade Tree reissued a remaster on October 16, 2001, which is how most fans found it.

years.h: The Only Reason I Feel Secure EP
years.p: Pedro the Lion's second EP, co-released by Made in Mexico and Jade Tree.

years.h: Song A / Song B for the Sub Pop Singles Club
years.p: A 1,300-copy single for Sub Pop's subscription series.

years.h: Winners Never Quit: a corrupt politician's rise and fall
years.p: Pedro's first concept album, Jade Tree JT1046. Bazan played every instrument, and Pitchfork's 4.1 review got personal enough that he called it ad hominem.
years.xp:
Bazan summed the record up as damnation for the arrogant, judgment for the judgmental. It aimed at hypocrisy in the church as much as in politics.

A Japanese bonus track is an alternate take of the opener featuring Ben Gibbard.

years.h: Ben Gibbard plays bass in Pedro the Lion
years.p: The [[Death Cab for Cutie|0039c7ae-e1a7-4a7d-9b49-0cbc716821a6]] singer took the bass for a stretch in 2000. Two future [[Fleet Foxes|fa97dd36-1b82-43d7-a6e4-2adeafd59cef]] members also passed through the band before that group formed.

years.h: Progress / A Guitar for Janie, with a storybook
years.p: Suicide Squeeze pressed 2,000 copies of the single packaged with a storybook.

eras.title: Control, and the fans who objected
eras.text: Control was Pedro's heaviest record and its bleakest story: a cheating businessman murdered by his wife. Some of Bazan's Christian audience turned on him, and by Achilles Heel he was losing the faith they'd assumed he shared.

years.h: Control: an affair, a murder, and American capitalism
years.p: A businessman cheats and his wife kills him. Inspired by the 1999 WTO protests, it hit No. 36 on the independent chart, with [[Casey Foubert|739b77af-80b8-4896-ac4c-e8a922c9390a]] on bass.
years.xp:
Stereogum called it the heaviest Pedro the Lion album in tone and sound: distorted guitars, synths, big drums. Aaron Sprinkle helped engineer and mix.

Bazan said it wasn't autobiographical, just his disappointment with how the world works. Metacritic averaged it at 75.

q: Oh... they like the fast songs.
years.h: Jade Tree wanted fast songs; Bazan didn't get it
years.p: Bazan later told Stereogum part of Control's heaviness came from label pressure for faster material he never quite understood.
years.xp: On the Control tour, some Christian fans openly objected to the darker, more cynical songs. Wikipedia describes the fanbase as divided by the record.

years.h: Pedro the Lion appears in a Christian rock documentary
years.p: Bazan is featured in Why Should the Devil Have All the Good Music?, the 2004 documentary about faith and rock.

years.h: Achilles Heel: TW Walsh joins, reviews split
years.p: [[TW Walsh|80eb65f4-5a8f-4aaa-8bcd-4961b55f5971]] co-wrote Keep Swinging and wrote Start Without Me. Pitchfork gave 4.7; AllMusic gave 4.5 out of 5.
years.xp: Bazan called it less bleak and more multi-faceted than Control. It reached No. 26 on Heatseekers and No. 24 on the independent chart.

years.h: Bazan starts Headphones on the side
years.p: Bazan started the side band Headphones in 2005, the year before he retired the Pedro the Lion name.

eras.title: The brand name of his dysfunction
eras.text: Bazan ended Pedro the Lion in early 2006 and went out under his own name. His solo debut, Curse Your Branches, laid out his break with Christianity, and for years he made more money playing alone.

q: The brand name of my dysfunction more than anything else.
years.h: Pedro the Lion ends; David Bazan goes solo
years.p: The split was announced in early January 2006 and was amicable. TW Walsh went back to web development and his band The Soft Drugs.
years.xp: Bazan later told Stereogum he'd needed distance to understand why he couldn't hold a lineup together. He'd written 90 to 100 percent of the material, and tension with Walsh had driven Walsh out; they later made up.

years.h: Curse Your Branches: Bazan's record about leaving Christianity
years.p: His Barsuk solo debut documented his loss of faith. It debuted at No. 1 on Heatseekers and No. 116 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: TW Walsh remasters the Pedro catalog for vinyl
years.p: Walsh, back on good terms with Bazan, remastered the Pedro the Lion albums for reissue.

years.h: Bazan joins the band Overseas
years.p: With [[Will Johnson|9e455882-2bb2-47fa-b1ce-f8516123649d]] of Centro-matic and Bubba and Matt Kadane of Bedhead and [[The New Year|b3d5b1c9-95df-42ea-83eb-c86b18f61f8d]].

eras.title: Coming home to the old name
eras.text: Tired of touring alone, Bazan put a band back together and gave it the old name. The comeback became a planned five-album autobiography starting with his Phoenix childhood.

years.h: Pedro the Lion returns after eleven years
years.p: Bazan announced the reformation on October 4, 2017, with Erik Walters and Terence Ankeny. The first shows came that December.
years.xp:
Bazan said he missed the energy of playing with others and that touring alone had started to sting. Getting back in a band felt a bit like coming home.

He'd told Stereogum that same year he made three times as much playing shows solo as with Pedro.

years.h: Phoenix: first of a five-album autobiography
years.p: The first Pedro album in 15 years, on Polyvinyl, is about Bazan's Arizona childhood: bikes, model homes, desert. It went No. 1 on Heatseekers.

years.h: Strange Negotiations, the David Bazan documentary
years.p: Brandon Vedder's film follows Bazan's spiritual and personal turmoil against the 2016 election. Pedro the Lion provided the music.

years.h: Havasu, a surprise second chapter
years.p: Part two of Bazan's autobiography cycle, released on Polyvinyl without warning.

years.h: Santa Cruz, chapter three
years.p: The third installment of the autobiography cycle on Polyvinyl. That September Pedro covered B by [[Lync|65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355]] for a Suicide Squeeze split.

years.h: Pedro the Lion joins Grandaddy's Sophtware Slump tour
years.p: Stereogum announced the band as support on [[Grandaddy|9d4c4835-c71a-4647-a4fc-263e26832cd0]]'s 25th anniversary tour for The Sophtware Slump.
